extracted.intended_audience: funding agencies, research institutions, publishers, metrics providers, and researchers involved in research assessment and grant/hiring/promotion decisions
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for designing and using research-assessment rubrics that avoid reliance on journal-based metrics and instead evaluate research content, diverse outputs, and transparent criteria — targeted at funders, institutions, publishers, metrics suppliers, and researchers. Emphasizes what to avoid and concrete recommendations for each stakeholder class.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not use journal-based metrics (Journal Impact Factors) as a proxy for research quality
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not use journal-based metrics, such as Journal Impact Factors, as a surrogate measure of the quality of individual research articles, to assess an individual scientist's contributions, or in hiring, promotion, or funding decisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicit anti-principle covering hiring, promotion, tenure, funding, and individual researcher assessment; instructs decision-makers to avoid using JIFs as a proxy for article or researcher quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be explicit about the criteria used to evaluate scientific productivity (funders)
rubrics_metrics.description: Be explicit about the criteria used in evaluating the scientific productivity of grant applicants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Funders should state clearly what measures and evidence they will use when assessing applicants (e.g., types of outputs counted, time windows, qualitative evidence) to promote transparency and fairness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emphasize scientific content over publication metrics for early-stage investigators (funders)
rubrics_metrics.description: Highlight, especially for early-stage investigators, that the scientific content of a paper is much more important than publication metrics or the journal in which it was published.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When evaluating early-career applicants, prioritize the novelty, rigor, and contribution of the work itself rather than venue prestige or citation counts; explicitly signal this to reviewers and applicants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider value and impact of all research outputs (funders)
rubrics_metrics.description: Consider value and impact of all research outputs (including datasets and software) in addition to research publications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Grant rubrics should credit and assess non-traditional outputs (data, code, protocols, software, policy briefs), include acceptable forms of evidence for these outputs, and weigh them alongside articles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider a broad range of impact measures including qualitative indicators (funders)
rubrics_metrics.description: Consider broad range of impact measures including qualitative indicators (influence on policy/practice).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use both qualitative (case studies, policy citations, practice uptake) and quantitative indicators (citations, altmetrics) and avoid over-reliance on single numerical indicators.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be explicit about criteria for hiring/tenure/promotion (institutions)
rubrics_metrics.description: Be explicit about criteria used to reach hiring, tenure, promotion decisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Institutions should publish the criteria and evidence they expect and how different outputs and activities are evaluated to ensure transparency and reduce hidden biases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Highlight scientific content over publication metrics (institutions)
rubrics_metrics.description: Highlight scientific content over publication metrics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Committees should prioritize the substance, rigor, and contribution of work during personnel decisions and avoid using journal prestige as a shortcut.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider value and impact of all research outputs (institutions)
rubrics_metrics.description: Consider value and impact of all research outputs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Academic promotion and hiring rubrics should recognize datasets, software, methodological contributions, and other non-article outputs explicitly and provide guidance on how to document them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Greatly reduce emphasis on the journal impact factor (publishers)
rubrics_metrics.description: Greatly reduce emphasis on the journal impact factor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publishers should stop promoting JIF as a primary measure of journal quality and avoid using it in ways that drive assessment of individual articles or authors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide a range of article-level metrics (publishers)
rubrics_metrics.description: Make available a range of article-level metrics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publishers should expose diverse, transparent article-level indicators (usage, citations, altmetrics, contextual information) rather than relying on journal-level aggregates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Encourage responsible authorship practices (publishers)
rubrics_metrics.description: Encourage responsible authorship practices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publishers should adopt and promote clear authorship and contributorship standards (e.g., contributor roles) to ensure accountability and accurate attribution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Remove reuse limitations on reference lists for transparency (publishers)
rubrics_metrics.description: Remove all reuse limitations on reference lists for transparency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allow unrestricted reuse of reference metadata to facilitate assessment, citation analysis, and transparency of scholarly work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Base personnel decisions on scientific content not publication metrics (researchers)
rubrics_metrics.description: Make personnel-related decisions based on scientific content rather than publication metrics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Researchers serving on hiring, promotion, or grant panels should evaluate the merits and substance of contributions, not journal prestige or raw citation counts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cite primary literature rather than reviews where possible (researchers)
rubrics_metrics.description: Cite primary literature rather than reviews when possible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer original sources to reviews to ensure credit to primary contributions and to make assessments of individual work clearer.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use a range of article metrics and indicators (researchers)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use a range of article metrics and indicators.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When considering impact, combine quantitative and qualitative indicators and contextualize metrics rather than taking any single metric at face value.

rubrics_metrics.name: Challenge inappropriate research assessment practices (researchers)
rubrics_metrics.description: Challenge research assessment practices that rely inappropriately on JIFs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Individuals should speak up and work to change local practices that depend on journal-based metrics for evaluating people or work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be open and transparent about data and methods (metrics suppliers)
rubrics_metrics.description: Be open and transparent about data and methods.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Suppliers of bibliometric and other metrics must make their data sources, algorithms, and methods publicly available and documented so users can interpret indicators properly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide data with no reuse restrictions and computational access (metrics suppliers)
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide data with no restrictions on reuse; provide computational access.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Metrics providers should allow unrestricted reuse of data and provide APIs or bulk access to enable independent verification and analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid JIF-based proxy assessment (implication/anti-pattern)
rubrics_metrics.description: JIF-based proxy assessment — using journal impact factor to judge individual articles or researchers — should be avoided.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicit anti-pattern: do not translate journal-level metrics into individual-level judgments; implement rubrics that evaluate the article/researcher directly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid single-metric reductive evaluation (implication/anti-pattern)
rubrics_metrics.description: Single-metric reductive evaluation — relying on one number to represent research quality or impact — should be avoided.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design rubrics that combine multiple indicators and qualitative evidence; beware of unintended incentives from single-number assessments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid hidden weighting of journal prestige (implication/anti-pattern)
rubrics_metrics.description: Hidden weighting of journal prestige in assessment decisions should be avoided.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make any weighting explicit or eliminate weighting that privileges venue prestige; ensure reviewers disclose and follow stated criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid implicit valuation of 'high-impact' venues (implication/anti-pattern)
rubrics_metrics.description: Implicit valuation of 'high-impact' venues as proxies for research quality should be avoided.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure rubrics and evaluation processes do not implicitly reward publication in certain named journals without assessing content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluate research content directly (DORA-aligned rubric requirement)
rubrics_metrics.description: A DORA-aligned grant rubric must evaluate research content directly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assessment criteria should require reviewers to read and judge the substance of work (rigor, novelty, contribution) and provide guidance on evidence and documentation expected.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider diverse research outputs (DORA-aligned rubric requirement)
rubrics_metrics.description: A DORA-aligned grant rubric must consider diverse research outputs (papers, data, software, policy briefs).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide explicit categories and examples of acceptable outputs and guidance on how to present and evaluate non-article contributions in applications and CVs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use qualitative AND quantitative indicators (DORA-aligned rubric requirement)
rubrics_metrics.description: A DORA-aligned grant rubric must use qualitative AND quantitative indicators.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Combine peer judgment, narrative impact statements, case studies, and multiple numerical indicators; require contextualization of metrics presented by applicants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be transparent about applied criteria (DORA-aligned rubric requirement)
rubrics_metrics.description: A DORA-aligned grant rubric must be transparent about the criteria applied.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publish the rubric, scoring guidance, and how different outputs and indicators are weighted or interpreted; transparency enables accountability and applicant guidance.
